title: Normal intracranial anatomy: spatial observations
author: NeuroImage example curriculum (unreviewed)
objective: Relate true source MRI sections to native 3D surfaces using physical section guides and selective transparency. Describe source-defined spatial relationships, check them in adjacent sections, and preserve a reproducible view with its evidence limits.

scenes.title: 1. Locate the same source point in 2D and 3D
scenes.prompt: Locate the selected left caudate label and its marker in the three MRI planes. Enable one section guide at a time and relate its position to the 3D source surfaces. Move through adjacent slices, then return to the recorded view. Which information comes from MRI, which from the source labels, and which from the schematic guides?
scenes.note: Colored guide planes identify displayed section positions within the image field of view. They contain no MRI texture or tissue and do not establish an anatomical boundary.

scenes.title: 2. Inspect deep labels within tissue context
scenes.prompt: Rotate the source surfaces while retaining the putamen as the selected region. Change only the opacity of the cerebral white-matter context and observe which spatial relationships become easier to see. Verify any proposed relationship in the T2 sections at the same physical location.
scenes.note: The white-matter label is a categorical tissue region, not an individual fiber pathway or cortical surface. Transparency is a display operation, not dissection, tissue removal or evidence of a tract.

scenes.title: 3. Compare adjacent deep source definitions
scenes.prompt: Identify the selected external pallidal label, then compare its position with the delivered putamen, caudate and thalamic parcellation union. Describe the relationship separately in axial, coronal and sagittal views. Explain where MRI alone is insufficient to establish a categorical boundary.
scenes.note: The thalamic context is a computed union of explicit source values. It is not a newly segmented whole thalamus, and no missing source value is filled. Consult each source definition before interpreting extent.

scenes.title: 4. Relate cortical labels to the visible folds
scenes.prompt: Follow the delivered precentral and postcentral labels across adjacent MRI sections. Rotate the two surfaces and use the sagittal guide to relate the 3D view to the section location. State which folds you can observe and which region assignments depend on the source parcellation.
scenes.note: These are source parcellation regions. Their boundaries do not establish individual functional localization. Guide planes describe imaging orientation, not sulcal or functional boundaries.

scenes.title: 5. Observe the represented ventricular spaces
scenes.prompt: Begin at the selected third-ventricular source point. Relate the separately delivered lateral and fourth ventricular labels to the brainstem context in 2D and 3D. Use adjacent sections to evaluate apparent gaps. What remains unresolved at this source resolution?
scenes.note: The display does not infer anatomical continuity from a surface connection or a sampling gap. The source Pons entry has a narrower definition in its metadata; inspect that definition rather than assuming complete coverage.

scenes.title: 6. Inspect brainstem and cerebellar source coverage
scenes.prompt: Inspect the selected source Pons region with the fourth-ventricular and cerebellar context. Make one cerebellar union opaque, then translucent, and explain how that affects visibility without changing anatomy. Use all three MRI sections to check the relationship you describe. Record a limitation in your teaching notes.
scenes.note: The cerebellar unions combine delivered parcellations and have incomplete source-value coverage. They do not provide a complete folial or nuclear atlas. Some brainstem structures are separately labelled and are excluded from the selected categorical region.
